headline: Computational models link tumour vasculature, drug transport and immune dynamics
label: Computational Tumour Therapy Models
summary: Patient-specific and agent-based tumour models now quantify how immunotherapy, antibody-drug conjugates and vasculature shape therapy response.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational frameworks for solid tumours in which spatial transport, cell-population dynamics and drug mechanism are represented explicitly. A PDE framework couples tumour and CTL immune dynamics with TGF-β chemotaxis and is simulated on patient-specific 3D geometry derived from brain scans for glioblastoma immunotherapy. An agent-based hybrid model, SimADC, separates target-dependent from target-independent antibody-drug conjugate killing and scales from mice to humans. A blood-flow and oxygen-transport model with an oxygen-dependent drug (T-DM1) shows that compressed, abnormal vessels reduce overlap between drug and oxygen. What is new is the explicit separation of mechanistic contributions to efficacy, expressed as predictions for therapy. The three items differ in scale and scope, so this thread is dominant rather than shared by every item.
